seo.title: Borrowing
seo.description: Definica's borrowing markets: osETH as the primary collateral, rules set per market, the health factor and liquidation explained, and the 75/25 interest split.

hero.title:
Borrow with the 
rules up front.
hero.text: Post approved ETH-correlated collateral, with osETH as the primary collateral asset, and borrow a supported asset. Each market sets its own collateral, oracle, limits and liquidation process, and the app shows them before you confirm.

markets.title:
Who brings 
what.
markets.intro: Liquidity flows into a market from two sources, borrowers take loans from it, and the interest they pay is split between the liquidity behind it and Definica.

participants.title: Borrowers
participants.bears: Interest, oracle risk and liquidation risk

participants.title: Funding loans
participants.brings: The proceeds of a funding loan, through the Main Liquidity Module
participants.bears: Funding cost, lending losses and liquidation risk at Aave

participants.title: Direct ETH supply
participants.brings: Their own ETH, with no Aave funding debt
participants.bears: Lending losses; exits follow the market's withdrawal conditions

markets.asset: Each market lends a supported asset, listed with the market in the app. Liquidity from funding loans arrives as the asset borrowed at Aave: WETH or another permitted asset.

collateral.title:
Nothing is collateral 
by default.
collateral.intro: A market enables each collateral asset explicitly, and only for itself. Committing aEthosETH to the Main Liquidity Module doesn't make it collateral.

items.title: osETH
items.text: The primary collateral asset of the borrowing markets.

items.title: aEthosETH
items.text: Collateral only in a market that approves it, under that market's own oracle, LTV, liquidity, lock, redemption and liquidation rules.

items.title: Other ETH-correlated assets
items.text: Collateral in any market that approves them, under that market's own rules.

paths.title: One aEthosETH receipt, two paths

items.title: As collateral
items.text: Where a market approves aEthosETH, you post it and borrow against it, under that market's rules.

items.title: As liquidity
items.text: Committed in the Main Liquidity Module, it backs a funding loan that supplies the market. You are then a liquidity participant, not a borrower.

paths.note: A single aEthosETH position doesn't serve both paths at once, unless a market's rules provide for it.

parameters.title:
What each 
parameter sets.
parameters.intro: Every market is defined by the same parameters. Their values are set per market: the app lists them for each market, and the review repeats the ones that apply before you confirm.

items.title: Supported borrow asset
items.text: The asset borrowers receive and repay, in which the debt and its interest are counted.

items.title: Approved collateral assets
items.text: The assets you can post. osETH is the primary one; nothing is collateral unless the market approves it.

items.title: Oracle
items.text: How collateral and debt are valued: the price source, how a stale or failed price is handled, and how often the value updates.

items.title: Maximum LTV
items.text: The most you can borrow, as a percentage of your collateral's value. A limit, not a target to borrow up to.

items.title: Liquidation threshold
items.text: The loan-to-value at which a position becomes eligible for liquidation. The gap below it is your cushion.

items.title: Interest-rate model
items.text: How the borrow rate responds to utilisation, and how much of the interest reaches lenders.

items.title: Market caps
items.text: The limits on total supply and total borrowing. A reached cap blocks new supply or new loans.

items.title: Liquidation process
items.text: Who may liquidate, how much of the debt one liquidation can repay, the liquidator's compensation and any liquidation fee.

items.title: Health monitoring
items.text: How positions are watched, and how borrowers are warned as they approach the threshold.

items.title: Liquidity management
items.text: How lenders' withdrawals are served, and what happens when utilisation is high.

items.title: Debt attribution
items.text: How loans, interest and losses are attributed to the liquidity behind them.

items.title: Emergency controls
items.text: Which controls exist, such as a pause, caps or a migration, and who can use them.

items.title: Contracts and network
items.text: The market's contract addresses and the network they run on, listed in the app and checkable onchain.

items.title: Activation conditions
items.text: What must hold for the market to accept supply and new loans.

items.title: The cushion
items.text: Compare the maximum LTV with the liquidation threshold. A small gap means a small price move, or a little accrued interest, can make a position liquidatable.

items.title: The oracle
items.text: A position is liquidated on the oracle's price, which can differ from the price you see elsewhere.

items.title: Rates and caps
items.text: Near a borrow cap or at high utilisation, the borrow rate can rise quickly and lenders' withdrawals can wait.

items.title: Emergency powers
items.text: Check who can pause or cap the market, and whether a delay applies before a change takes effect.

items.title: The onchain values
items.text: If the app, the docs and the deployed contracts ever differ, the contract state prevails.

health.title:
Liquidation, 
in plain words.
health.intro: Your health factor compares what your collateral counts for with what you owe. Above 1 the position stands; below 1 it can be liquidated.

items.title: The collateral's value falls
items.text: osETH's market price or exchange rate can fall relative to the debt asset.

items.title: The debt grows
items.text: Variable interest accrues continuously, faster at high utilisation, with no price move at all.

items.title: The oracle disagrees
items.text: The market values collateral on its oracle's price, which can lag or differ from prices elsewhere.

items.title: The rules change
items.text: Governance can change thresholds and leave an existing position closer to liquidation.

liquidation.title: Below 1
liquidation.text: Liquidators repay part or all of the debt and take collateral at a discount, their bonus. Any liquidation fee is separate from the repayment and the bonus. A liquidation reduces the position; it doesn't necessarily clear the debt.

cushion.title: Keep a cushion
cushion.text: The gap between the maximum LTV and the liquidation threshold is the room between the most you can borrow and the point of liquidation. Borrowing to the maximum leaves a thin cushion.

lending.title:
Interest, split 
75 / 25.
lending.intro: Borrowers pay interest. Of the lending interest attributable to you as a liquidity participant, 75% is allocated to you and 25% to Definica.

split.caption: Of the lending interest attributable to you

points.title: Before your costs
points.text: Definica's share is taken on attributable lending interest before upstream financing costs: never on your principal, never on net profit.

points.title: Attributable means yours
points.text: It follows how much lending balance you supplied and for how long. LTV is a borrowing constraint, not an allocation key.

points.title: Other returns stay apart
points.text: The osETH staking return, Aave supply interest and lock incentives are not part of the split; each has its own line.

points.title: It can be negative
points.text: Financed, your result is 75% of attributable interest minus funding costs and other applicable costs. If the loan costs more, you lose money even though the market earned interest.

points.title: Direct supply
points.text: Supplying your own ETH carries no funding cost, but the same market risks: lending losses, utilisation and liquidity.

points.title: Definica's share
points.text: It supports development, operations and budgeted treasury and incentive programmes.

rules.title:
Four rules that 
always apply.
rules.intro: Whatever a market's parameters are set to, these four hold in every one of them.

items.title: Debt and interest
items.text: Borrowers pay interest, and the debt with its accrued interest must be repaid to release the collateral.

items.title: Oracle dependency
items.text: An oracle prices the collateral and the borrow asset. Its correctness is a dependency of every market.

items.title: Liquidation
items.text: If the collateral's value falls, the debt grows or the position crosses its threshold, some or all of the collateral can be sold.

items.title: Correlation is not safety
items.text: ETH-correlated collateral still carries validator, fee, price, liquidity, redemption and contract risks.

risks.title:
What can 
go wrong.
risks.intro: Borrowing and lending carry different risks. Both sides are set out here.

items.title: Losing collateral
items.text: Borrowing instead of selling doesn't guarantee you keep the collateral: some or all of it can be sold in a liquidation.

items.title: Debt that grows
items.text: Variable interest accrues continuously, and a position that started healthy can drift towards its threshold without any price move.

items.title: Bad debt
items.text: If a borrower's collateral is sold too late or too cheaply to cover the debt, the shortfall falls on lenders.

items.title: Utilisation
items.text: When most of a market's liquidity is lent out, withdrawals wait until borrowers repay or new liquidity arrives.

items.title: Market insolvency
items.text: A market-wide event can leave more debt than collateral.

items.title: Funding cost
items.text: A financed participant owes Aave whatever the market returns, so lending losses and funding costs can outweigh returns.

closing.title:
Read the market, 
then borrow.
closing.text: Each market's collateral, oracle, maximum LTV, liquidation threshold and caps are shown in the app before you confirm. The documentation explains each one in full.
